input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 gives either Party a convenience exit on 90 days' written notice against a one-year auto-renewing term, which sits at our fallback on notice period and on HDI's symmetrical (end-of-term) right — that element we do not redline. The material failure is Section 4.2: if the Company terminates, it owes an uncapped Termination Payment equal to 50% of Net Sales above $800,000 for the trailing twelve months, payable over eight quarterly installments. Because fees to HDI are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month, that formula can exceed a full year's fees and far exceeds the fallback ceiling of three months' fees, so the Company has no genuinely penalty-free exit. We therefore capped the Termination Payment at three months' fees (fallback rather than preferred, given HDI's site build investment and the revenue-share bargain).

ops.oldText: the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: the balance of which shall be divided by two; provided, that in no event shall the Termination Payment exceed an amount equal to the aggregate fees payable by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months immediately preceding the Termination Date.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We capped the Termination Payment at three months' fees, since as drafted it is an uncapped share of Net Sales that operates as a penalty on a routine non-renewal. Our playbook position is termination for convenience without penalty; the three-month cap is our fallback and reflects HDI's build investment.
proposal.summary: Cap the Company's Termination Payment at three months' fees.
